Int64.description: 64-bit signed integer; `Int` aliases the platform word size. Overflow wraps silently — use `checked_add` or BigInt when that matters.

Float64.description: IEEE-754 double. `Float32` and `Float16` also exist; literals default to Float64.

Bool.description: true or false. A subtype of Integer, so `true + true == 2`.

Char.description: A single Unicode code point, written with single quotes.

String.description: Immutable UTF-8 text. Indexing is by byte offset, so iterate with `eachindex` or `graphemes` rather than 1:length.

Symbol.description: An interned name, written `:name`. Used for keys and metaprogramming; cheaper to compare than String.

Array.description: Dense N-dimensional array, column-major. `Vector{T}` is `Array{T,1}`, `Matrix{T}` is `Array{T,2}`.

Dict.description: Hash map. `Dict(k => v, ...)`; iteration order is unspecified.

Tuple.description: Immutable fixed-length heterogeneous sequence. `NamedTuple` adds field names.

Missing.description: Type whose only instance is `missing`, for absent data.

AbstractArray.description: Supertype of array-likes. Write methods against this, not Array, to accept views and ranges.

Number.description: Root of the numeric hierarchy: Real -> Integer/AbstractFloat/Rational, plus Complex.

Function.description: Supertype of all callables. Every function has its own singleton type, which is how dispatch specialises.

Type.description: The type of a type, used to dispatch on a type argument itself.
